story: Vishnu rests on the serpent Shesha in the cosmic ocean, with Lakshmi at his feet. Whenever adharma rises, he descends as an avatar: the fish, the tortoise, the boar, Narasimha, Vamana, Parashurama, Rama, Krishna, the Buddha (in many lists), and Kalki, who is still to come.
belief: Vaishnavas worship Vishnu as the supreme god who protects the world and grants liberation through devotion. In the Bhagavad Gita, as Krishna, he promises to return age after age to protect the good.
turns: Even the preserver's choices have a cost. As Vamana he tricked the good king Mahabali out of his kingdom, and as the enchantress Mohini he cheated the asuras out of the nectar of immortality. Devotees see these as acts of cosmic balance; critics call them unfair.
facts: The Venkateswara temple at Tirupati, a form of Vishnu, is one of the most visited religious sites in the world.
The Vishnu Sahasranama lists 1,000 names of Vishnu.
Ekadashi, the 11th day of each lunar fortnight, is a fasting day dedicated to him.
